title: The option dealer's hedge is forced and its sign is knowable: when the dealer is short gamma its hedging is momentum, when long gamma it is mean reversion — so the tape predicts the sign of short-horizon autocorrelation, not direction

scout.mechanism: A dealer that has taken the other side of a customer's option must delta-hedge in the underlying, and it has no discretion about the direction: short an option it must buy as price rises and sell as it falls (its hedge amplifies moves); long an option it must sell into rallies and buy dips (its hedge damps them). The magnitude of that forced trading per unit of price move is gamma, and its sign is the sign of the dealer's net option position. This repository's gold tape carries the customer's side explicitly — flow_class is LC/SC/LP/SP, 20,724 prints over seven sessions and growing ~3,500 a day — so the dealer's position is the arithmetic inverse of the tape, no aggressor inference required, and strike, expiration, dte, contracts and underlying_price are on every row. The claim is therefore NOT about direction. It is that in minutes when the near-dated book is net short gamma, one-minute returns in the underlying are positively autocorrelated, and when it is net long gamma they are negatively autocorrelated — the dealer's hedge is a mechanical feedback loop whose sign flips with its inventory. This is an economically different object from every one of the thirty-one closed records, all of which tested a direction, a drift or a level; a claim about the sign of autocorrelation cannot be produced by any chart pattern because it is a statement about who is forced to trade against the next tick.
scout.why_unarbitraged: Three reasons, none of them 'nobody thought of it'. (1) The people best placed to see this are the dealers doing the hedging, and they cannot stop hedging — a delta-hedged book is a regulatory and risk-management obligation, not a trade, so the flow is price-insensitive by construction and the dealer profits from the spread it charged, not from suppressing the footprint. (2) In equities this mechanism is packaged and sold (SpotGamma, Menthor, the daily 'GEX' note); in gold it is not, because there is no free consolidated options tape, the underlying is a five-active-month futures complex whose open interest must be stitched from CME daily bulletins, and the one commercial feed that classifies customer side (live.otldata.com, already paid for and already ingested here) is undocumented enough that this repository had to discover by correlation scan that its timestamps were seven hours off (docs/decisions/2026-09-12-otl-timestamps.md). That is awkward, not secret, which is exactly the shape the brief points at. (3) Even fully known, the mechanism is not a free directional bet that a counterparty can fade away: it says a trade held for minutes should be managed as trend in one state and as reversion in the other. Knowing it does not create an offsetting flow, because the offsetting flow would have to be the dealer declining to hedge.
data_needed: data/gold/tape/date=*/ — ON DISK: 20,724 COMEX gold option prints, 2026-09-06 to 2026-09-15, with flow_class (LC/SC/LP/SP = the customer's side), strike, expiration, dte, contracts, trade_price, underlying_price, premium_usd. Timestamps corrected to UTC per 2026-09-12-otl-timestamps.md.

data/bars/GC-1m.parquet — ON DISK: 8,664 one-minute bars of the tape's own underlying, same feed, same clock, exactly the tape's window. This is the return series; no cross-venue alignment is involved anywhere, which is what 2026-09-15-venue-residual said any successor must guarantee.

NOT ON DISK, and the proposal must say so: implied_volatility is null on 100% of rows and there are no flags (flag_block/sweep/multi_leg/spread are all zero). Delta and gamma must be computed with Black-76 from trade_price, strike, dte and underlying_price, backing IV out per print. That is arithmetic, not a new feed, but it is work and it introduces a modelling choice that must be frozen before the run.

NOT ON DISK, and OPTIONAL: CME daily bulletin gold option open interest by strike (free CSV, cmegroup.com/daily_bulletin). Without it the dealer's inventory is proxied by cumulative signed flow since 2026-09-06, which misses pre-existing open interest. Defensible for near-dated gamma, which is dominated by recent near-the-money flow, but it is the assumption the adversary should attack first.

Vantage XAUUSD.sc costs for the trading leg (config/default.toml: spread 0.28, swap 0.00). The basis objection in config/default.toml — 'spot XAUUSD trades tens of dollars below GC, wider than the strike spacing' — blocks attaching LEVELS from this tape to the spot market. It does not block this claim: an autocorrelation of returns is invariant to a slowly varying basis, and the two series correlate at 0.9867 on one-minute log returns (2026-09-12-otl-timestamps.md).
scout.falsifier_sketch: Declare before the run: (a) the gamma state variable — net dealer gamma of the book with dte <= 7, signed so that positive means the dealer is LONG gamma; (b) the statistic — the first-order autocorrelation of one-minute GC log returns computed separately in the top and bottom terciles of the state variable, with the state variable lagged one minute so nothing contemporaneous enters; (c) the declared direction, with no mirror available — short-gamma minutes have HIGHER autocorrelation than long-gamma minutes. It dies if the difference (rho_short_gamma - rho_long_gamma) is <= 0, or if it is positive but fails to reach the 95th percentile of a null that permutes the gamma state across minutes within the same hour-of-day and the same realised-volatility decile (both controls are required: the tape's flow concentrates in the New York morning, so an hour-matched null is mandatory per the standing rule in BACKLOG.md, and gamma correlates with volatility). It also dies, regardless of the percentile, if the SAME test run on a placebo state variable built from the tape's total premium traded — a pure activity measure carrying no gamma sign — produces a difference of the same sign and within a factor of two of the same size; that would mean the result is 'busy minutes trend' wearing a costume. Power must be declared, not discovered: state the minimum detectable rho difference at n minutes before opening the window, and if seven sessions cannot reach it the honest verdict is 'not yet', not 'no'. The out-of-sample window should be named as a FUTURE date range — this tape accrues ~1,400 unread minutes a day, which is the only genuinely unread out-of-sample data this repository has ever had.
scout.closest_known: docs/research/BACKLOG.md, 'Options: cluster-at-level with the accumulated tape — blocked until the collector has months of tape', and the founding thesis recorded in docs/decisions/2026-09-13-night-synthesis.md as 'options flow at levels'. That claim is directional and spatial: a cluster of prints at a strike acts as support or resistance and price moves to or through it. This one is neither directional nor spatial — it never looks at where a strike sits relative to price, it asks only whether the dealer's aggregate position makes its hedging pro-cyclical or counter-cyclical, and the thing predicted is a second moment of the return series rather than its sign. The practical consequence of that difference is the reason this is worth running now: a level claim needs enough DISTINCT levels to be visited, which is months of tape, while an autocorrelation claim's unit of observation is a minute, and 8,664 aligned minutes already exist. Second closest: docs/decisions/2026-09-15-venue-residual.md, which closed with the rule that no comparison may be registered at bar resolution when the quantity measured is smaller than the misalignment. That rule is respected here by construction — tape and bars come from one feed on one clock, and the measured quantity (a minute-scale autocorrelation) is an order of magnitude larger than the one-minute stamping granularity, not twenty times smaller than it.
